Vestas Wind Systems A/S Unveils New Turbine Model in Push for Higher Efficiency

COPENHAGEN, June 20—Danish renewable energy company Vestas Wind Systems A/S launched a new onshore wind turbine model Thursday, aiming to boost energy output and lower costs for developers as global demand for clean power accelerates.

The new V180-6.5 MW turbine, announced at the company’s headquarters in Aarhus, offers a larger rotor diameter and higher capacity than previous models. According to Vestas, the turbine is designed for low and medium-wind sites, and can deliver up to 8% more annual energy production compared to its predecessor.

“With the V180-6.5 MW, we’re responding directly to our customers’ need for higher productivity and efficient land use,” said Mikkel Jensen, Vestas’s Chief Technology Officer, at the launch event. “This turbine will help accelerate the energy transition by making wind power more competitive in markets worldwide.”

Industry analysts say the new turbine could strengthen Vestas’s position amid increasing competition from other wind technology manufacturers. “Scaling up capacity while maintaining reliability is crucial for developers looking to meet ambitious renewable targets,” said Anders Holm, analyst at the Danish Renewable Energy Association.

Vestas Wind Systems A/S stated that the new model will be available for orders in the third quarter of 2024, with deliveries expected to begin in 2026. The company also highlighted its commitment to sustainability, noting that the turbine’s components are designed for easier recycling at end-of-life.

The Danish government has set a target to generate 70% of its energy from renewables by 2030, with wind power playing a central role in meeting those goals.
